claims.claim: rooted plants release sediment-derived phosphorus mainly as they decay
claims.note: Full text not read. The abstract (Crossref) is consistent: 'Phosphorus release ... appears to be primarily dependent upon tissue decay rather than excretory processes'. Conditions from the abstract: a controlled-environment laboratory study in lucite columns separating sediment and roots from a P-free nutrient solution; three species (Egeria densa, Hydrilla verticillata, Myriophyllum spicatum, none native to Maine soft-water lakes) on five sediments, about 3 months. The paper states it as a general property of rooted plants; the rewrite should say 'in laboratory columns with three canopy-forming species'.
